segments.copy: If your stomach looks like this on a GLP-1, mine does too. I'm eating less, but some days I feel more bloated than ever.
segments.visual: H01: Same fictional adult woman throughout; clothed side profile in her bedroom mirror, then looks toward phone camera. Show clear persistent “Dramatized story” disclosure; no before/after.
segments.purpose: Immediate recognition; the word this has a visible referent.
segments.evidence: Fictional first-person dramatization; no actual customer account or Motilli use/result supplied. User hook; original illustrative staging

segments.copy: I can sit down to a small lunch, eat a few bites, and already feel that tightness across my stomach. I look at what's left on my plate and think, how am I this full?
segments.visual: H02: Overhead lunch plate; woman puts fork down beside a modest meal.
segments.purpose: Name the contradiction that earns the explanation.
segments.evidence: Fictional first-person dramatization; no actual customer account or Motilli use/result supplied. Audience scenario, not a testimonial

segments.copy: The worst part is getting dressed in the morning and feeling good in something, then wanting to peel it off by the afternoon because the waistband is digging into me.
segments.visual: H03: Seated three-quarter office view; discreet waistband adjustment beneath desk.
segments.purpose: Move from symptom to daily consequence.
segments.evidence: Fictional first-person dramatization; no actual customer account or Motilli use/result supplied. Original scenario informed by local bloating research

segments.copy: I wanted to feel comfortable in my clothes again. Instead, I'm standing sideways in the mirror before we go out, deciding whether I need a looser top.
segments.visual: H04: Hallway wide shot; woman pauses with handbag and keys, glances toward mirror.
segments.purpose: Establish the desired outcome: comfort and participation.
segments.evidence: Fictional first-person dramatization; no actual customer account or Motilli use/result supplied. Original scenario; not a measured audience prevalence claim

segments.copy: I've tried peppermint tea. I've gone back over what I ate, wondering whether it was the dairy, or the meal before that. Some days, it feels like every food becomes a suspect.
segments.visual: H05: Kitchen close overhead; her hand rests beside peppermint tea and a food diary. No product-failure montage or discarded medication.
segments.purpose: Acknowledge effort without declaring treatments ineffective.
segments.evidence: Fictional first-person dramatization; no actual customer account or Motilli use/result supplied. Conditional audience recognition

segments.copy: What finally made me look at this differently was learning about GLP-1 gut slowdown. My shot could be changing how quickly food moved through my stomach.
segments.visual: P01: Same woman speaks to phone at kitchen table. At “GLP-1 gut slowdown”, add that exact short label; no diagnosis or medical costume.
segments.purpose: Introduce the selected mechanism as the answer to her unresolved question.
segments.evidence: V3 first-person fictional dramatization. Official Wegovy stomach-emptying context and NIDDK general stomach movement; not evidence of Motilli efficacy.

segments.copy: I'd been focused on how little I was eating. But medicines such as Wegovy can slow stomach emptying. That means food can stay in the stomach longer after a meal.
segments.visual: S01: Authentic Wegovy source on tablet, highlight slowed stomach emptying. First-person narration continues across source insert.
segments.purpose: Give the mechanism an identifiable factual source.
segments.evidence: V3 first-person fictional dramatization. Official Wegovy stomach-emptying context and NIDDK general stomach movement; not evidence of Motilli efficacy.

segments.copy: Normally, the muscles in my stomach mix the food and gradually move it into my small intestine. So digestion depends on that movement happening, even when the meal is small.
segments.visual: S02: Single isolated stomach-to-duodenum model with normal mixing and gradual passage. No total blockage, product, rotten food or shutdown.
segments.purpose: Explain the necessary physical process in ordinary language.
segments.evidence: V3 first-person fictional dramatization. Official Wegovy stomach-emptying context and NIDDK general stomach movement; not evidence of Motilli efficacy.

segments.copy: When the stomach takes longer to empty, that full feeling can hang around too. That could help explain why a small lunch was leaving me feeling so uncomfortable afterward.
segments.visual: S03: Distinct time-and-fullness schematic; one small-meal icon with elapsed-time indicator. No invented hourly measurements.
segments.purpose: Connect the mechanism to the small-lunch opening without diagnosing the narrator.
segments.evidence: V3 first-person fictional dramatization. Official Wegovy stomach-emptying context and NIDDK general stomach movement; not evidence of Motilli efficacy.

segments.copy: That was the part I'd been missing. Eating less and moving food through my stomach are two different things. I was watching the portion size without thinking about the slowdown.
segments.visual: H07: Side-on kitchen scene; woman looks from partly eaten meal to notes on tablet. No anatomy reuse or visual recovery.
segments.purpose: Land the belief shift once, using the opening lived detail.
segments.evidence: V3 first-person fictional dramatization. Official Wegovy stomach-emptying context and NIDDK general stomach movement; not evidence of Motilli efficacy.

segments.copy: It also changed how I thought about all those foods I'd been blaming. Changing what was on my plate didn't tell me whether slower stomach emptying was contributing to the bloating.
segments.visual: H08: Macro food diary; hand adds the question “Could stomach emptying matter?” beside existing meal notes. Distinct from tea overhead.
segments.purpose: Explain the limit of her prior investigation without claiming dietary approaches never work.
segments.evidence: V3 first-person fictional dramatization. Official Wegovy stomach-emptying context and NIDDK general stomach movement; not evidence of Motilli efficacy.

segments.copy: So I had a better question for my prescriber: could the slowdown be part of what I was feeling, and what digestive support would actually make sense alongside my medication?
segments.visual: P02: Over-shoulder phone note with that prescriber question. She writes it; no fabricated consultation, recommendation or endorsement.
segments.purpose: Turn understanding into a relevant solution search; do not imply a supplement reverses medication effects.
segments.evidence: V3 first-person fictional dramatization. Official Wegovy stomach-emptying context and NIDDK general stomach movement; not evidence of Motilli efficacy.

segments.copy: During that search, I looked at a formula with celery juice powder, prebiotic fiber, and chlorophyll. I wanted to understand what was in it before adding another thing to my routine.
segments.visual: I01: Three distinct labeled ingredient stations. Actual seller-listed ingredients; no product-induced stomach contractions.
segments.purpose: Connect ingredient consideration to the ongoing search.
segments.evidence: Seller-listed product facts; dramatized consideration, no claimed use or result.

segments.copy: I learned that prebiotic fiber provides food for bacteria in the gut. That helped me understand its purpose, while remembering that my own tolerance still mattered when I was already feeling bloated.
segments.visual: I02: Microscopic-style schematic of bacteria using fiber substrate; no good-versus-evil characters or instant gas disappearance.
segments.purpose: Give the technical term a job and retain the relevant limitation.
segments.evidence: General prebiotic role; not evidence of Motilli bloating efficacy

segments.copy: Chlorophyll was another name I recognized once I read about it: the green pigment in plants. This formula lists a related form called chlorophyllin, alongside the celery juice powder and fiber.
segments.visual: I03: Celery stalk macro transitions at Chlorophyll to distinct leaf-pigment macro with chlorophyllin label.
segments.purpose: Clarify names without inventing a prokinetic or gas-neutralizing action.
segments.evidence: Current ingredient list names sodium copper chlorophyllin

segments.copy: That formula is Motilli, a daily digestive-support gummy marketed for people on a GLP-1. It gave me a specific ingredient list and routine to review with my prescriber.
segments.visual: PR01: Actual current Motilli product page on phone; first spoken/visible brand reveal, then ingredients and directions. No prescriber endorsement implied.
segments.purpose: Introduce a concrete product for consideration; no proven prokinetic claim.
segments.evidence: Seller-listed product facts; dramatized consideration, no claimed use or result.

segments.copy: And honestly, I liked the idea of a gummy. When I'm already feeling full, another drink to mix or a capsule to swallow doesn't sound appealing. Chewing something felt more manageable.
segments.visual: PR02: Verified bottle and gummy product demonstration on neutral surface; hands open bottle and show gummy texture. Clearly product demonstration, not a customer trial.
segments.purpose: Answer format objection through convenience rather than absorption superiority.
segments.evidence: Fictional first-person dramatization; no actual customer account or Motilli use/result supplied. Gummy format; hypothetical preference

segments.copy: The directions are two gummies before bed with a full glass of water. That's a routine I can picture fitting into my evening, alongside brushing my teeth and getting ready for bed.
segments.visual: PR03: Close-up verified printed or online directions at Two gummies, then distinct bedtime water-glass scene. Do not show narrator consuming product.
segments.purpose: Make use understandable without asserting universal medication compatibility.
segments.evidence: Current product directions; advise individual discussion

segments.copy: What I care about is how I actually feel. I'd want to keep track of the bloating and my comfort, so I could judge my own experience instead of guessing.
segments.visual: H06: Blank symptom journal, headings Bloating and Comfort; hand sets pen alongside it. No invented outcome tracking or elapsed treatment timeline.
segments.purpose: Replace borrowed week-by-week testimonial with a realistic evaluation.
segments.evidence: Fictional first-person dramatization; no actual customer account or Motilli use/result supplied. No timed outcome promise

segments.copy: I want to put on an outfit and leave it on. I want to enjoy dinner without quietly loosening my jeans underneath the table. Mostly, I want an evening where my stomach isn't taking up all my attention.
segments.visual: F01: Imagined social dinner, woman engaged with friends, no belly transformation. Clearly mark “What I want to get back to”; never show as a Motilli result.
segments.purpose: Resolve opening concerns as an aspiration, not a treatment result.
segments.evidence: Fictional first-person dramatization; no actual customer account or Motilli use/result supplied. Explicit aspirational framing

segments.copy: I've put the Motilli page below if you want to look at it too. You can see the ingredients, the directions, and the bottle options in one place.
segments.visual: PR04: Verified live product-page screen capture showing formula and bottle options; no price unless freshly checked.
segments.purpose: Make click destination specific and useful.
segments.evidence: Fictional first-person dramatization; no actual customer account or Motilli use/result supplied. Current product destination

segments.copy: The guarantee caught my attention as well. It's ninety days from delivery, and it includes opened bottles. So opening it doesn't take away the option to request a refund.
segments.visual: PR05: Real bottle with editor-rendered guarantee card: 90 days from delivery / Opened bottles included / Terms apply.
segments.purpose: State the actual risk reversal; no guaranteed result or no-return claim.
segments.evidence: Live refund policy checked 2026-09-09

segments.copy: If you're doing the same thing I am, checking your stomach and second-guessing every meal, you'll understand why I'm looking into this. Tap below to take a look at Motilli.
